Academic Recovery in 2024
• The availability of 2024 NHSAS data allows New Hampshire to
 update COVID-19 recovery analyses.
• Spring 2024 marks the third year since the pandemic began
 and this is the third report:
 • Summer 2021: Academic Impact
 • Summer 2022: Academic Recovery Year 1
 • Summer 2023: Academic Recovery Year 2
 • Summer 2024: Academic Recovery Year 3

 3

Two Types of Recovery in 2024: System & Student
• We elaborate on the results from the previous recovery analyses in two
 ways:
 • System level recovery: Is the education system supporting rates of
 learning that are comparable to what it was prior to the pandemic?
 • Student level recovery: Are students achieving at levels that are
 comparable to what they were prior to the pandemic?
• Previously, we focused mostly on system-level recovery: examining rates
 of learning in 2021 and 2022 compared to those prior to the pandemic.
• We continue examining system level analyses but also focus on student-
 level recovery.

 4

Two Types of Recovery: System & Student
• System-level recovery
 • Comparison of 2019 and 2024 same-grade student growth: We
 examined the change in baseline student growth (SGPs) for 2019
 students and 2024 students utilizing coefficient matrices derived
 from pre-pandemic cohorts of students.
• Student-level recovery
 • Comparison of 2019 to 2024 same-grade achievement: We
 examined the equipercentile change in achievement for 2019
 students and 2023 students at same-grade

 5

Student-level recovery
• It is critical to understand that recovery of the system does not imply
 student level recovery
• Because students’ rates of learning slowed so dramatically during the
 pandemic, rates of learning necessary to catch students up to where
 they would have been would have to be equally dramatic (in the positive
 direction)
• The following figures illustrate the extent to which student attainment is
 behind 2019 attainment levels.
• Comparison to 2019 levels is a “low bar” as attainment levels in 2024,
 had the pandemic not occurred, would almost certainly have been
 higher than 2019 levels (based on “typical” rates of yearly improvement)

Recovery Phase Year 1
• Student growth (baseline referenced to pre-pandemic rates of learning)
 was examined by content area and grade as well as for the major student
 demographic subgroups.
• Achievement (Student Recovery) and Growth (System Recovery) were
 characterized in three ways:
 • Lagging: Behind pre-pandemic levels (attainment or growth)
 • On Par: About the same as pre-pandemic levels (attainment or growth)
 • Leading: Ahead of pre-pandemic levels (attainment or growth)
• Because learning slowed during the initial phase of the pandemic, to make
 up for those losses, learning must accelerate to rates above normal (i.e.,
 leading)

Recovery Year 1
• Analysis of 2022 NHSAS & WIDA ACCESS data indicated two things:
 • Rates of learning, on average, have returned or are close returning to normal, pre-
 pandemic levels. That is, the system has more or less recovered.
 • Student attainment, on average, is still lagging behind because rates of learning have
 not accelerated enough to catch students up. That is, students have not recovered.
• In both ELA and mathematics, learning acceleration from the lows of the pandemic would
 be considered, on average, to be system stabilization.
• System stabilization (a return to normal rates of learning) will be insufficient to catch
 students up.
• Results from 2023 data will be important to assess the state of learning (beyond what the
 state experience pre-COVID) in New Hampshire.

 similar to the results in 2023.
• Student growth in mathematics in 2024 was slightly less than growth in 2019 and
 was less than growth observed in 2023.

Recovery Phase Year 2
• We again distinguish between student-level recovery and system-level
 recovery this year.
• Achievement (Student Recovery) and Growth (System Recovery) were
 characterized in three ways:
 • Lagging: Behind pre-pandemic levels
 • On Par: About the same as pre-pandemic levels
 • Leading: Ahead of pre-pandemic levels

 26

Recovery Phase Year 2
• Student growth in ELA in 2023 exceeded growth in 2022.
• Student growth in mathematics in 2023 was slightly less than growth in 2022.
• In both ELA and mathematics, growth remained above pre-pandemic levels (i.e.,
 50).
• This increase in rates of learning led to some groups closing the gap and slowly
 catching up with pre-pandemic levels of achievement.
• We are in the process of compiling results across the numerous states with whom
 the Center works. Thus far, New Hampshire appears to be performing better than
 many of the states in terms of accelerating student learning and, in turn, helping
 students recover.
